title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 32 (Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening)

content.overview: Section 32 provides that contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void.
content.glance: Contingent on event happening → enforceable only when event happens; void if event becomes impossible.
content.study: Contracts contingent on an uncertain future event happening cannot be enforced until the event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, the contracts become void. Current-law framing: identify the contingency of happening; test whether the event has happened or become impossible; apply enforceability or voidness.

sections.heading: Enforceable when event happens
sections.body: Cannot be enforced unless and until the uncertain future event has happened.

sections.heading: Void if impossible
sections.body: If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void.

provisions.title: Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening

examples.title: Event becomes impossible
examples.body: A contracts to pay B if a ship arrives. The ship is sunk. The contract becomes void under s. 32.

hypotheticals.question: Can the contract be enforced before the event?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 32: cannot be enforced unless and until the event has happened.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-32
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Contingent contracts are always void until the event happens.
misconceptions.correction: They are unenforceable until the event happens; they become void only if the event becomes impossible.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 32 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify contingency of happening. II. Test whether event happened or became impossible. III. Apply enforceability or voidness. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State both limbs: enforcement and voidness on impossibility.
